Built around the books you own

A little further.
A little more yours.

Your books. Your space. Your reading experience.

A native reading experience for iPhone and iPad, built around the books you own. Basic reading and library management should not depend on a subscription, a cloud service or an external library-management tool.

Last reviewed5 November 2026

Reviewed for our current launch plans and longer-term product direction.

Share a feature idea ↗
Direction, not a deadline.

This roadmap shares our direction, not guaranteed release commitments. Priorities, scope and order may change as we learn from readers and testing. No release dates or future prices are promised.

We are preparing Aflow Read’s first public App Store release. Explore the intended launch foundation below while final release checks are completed.

The launch foundation

Available Now

The first public App Store release is still being prepared. Here is a preview of its intended foundation. Released features will appear here once they are publicly available.

Public availability will be confirmed here when the first release is ready.

Prepared for the first release

Launch foundation · pending release

A comfortable EPUB reader

Portrait and landscape reading with Automatic, Single Page and Facing Pages. Columns adapt to usable reading width.

More about this direction
  • Reading appearance customization, progress and saved position.
  • Contents, supported text search, bookmarks and Go Back.
  • Supported illustrations and image navigation; availability depends on the EPUB.

Launch foundation · pending release

Your library, under your control

Import supported EPUB files or nested folders, browse and search your Bookshelf, and organize books into collections.

More about this direction
  • Multiple sources, source inspection and refresh.
  • Bring child-folder sources together under a parent while preserving existing book identity and reading state.
  • Metadata and cover overrides, removed-book recovery and local reading state.

Launch foundation · pending release

Native, adaptable layouts

Native iPhone and iPad interfaces that respond to the space available.

More about this direction
  • Layouts adapt to available reading space in portrait and landscape.
  • Device compatibility details will be confirmed alongside the public release.

Launch foundation · pending release

Free reading. Optional support.

The initial release is planned to be Free, with no subscription required.

More about this direction
  • Optional Buy Us a Coffee consumable support purchases are subject to final App Store qualification and unlock no additional reading features.
  • Lifetime Pro is not offered at the initial launch.
02

First development priority

Up Next

Broader reading formats, building on the current EPUB focus. Each format will be tested and refined before its support is confirmed.

Reading formats

PDF: build on existing support

Build on existing PDF import and reading support, with further work to complete and qualify the experience across a wider range of documents.

More about this direction
  • Reliable opening, rendering, fit/zoom and navigation.
  • Page-position persistence, supported bookmarks and library integration.
  • Test larger documents while keeping memory use predictable.

Reading formats

Plain text, thoughtfully presented

Explore TXT import and reading with dependable text handling and a place in your personal library.

More about this direction
  • Unicode and character-encoding handling.
  • Readable typography, navigation and saved progress.
  • Metadata integration and appropriate large-file behaviour.

Reading formats

Comics and image-based reading

Expand toward CBZ and suitable image collections. CBR support depends on compatibility and licensing evaluation.

More about this direction
  • Full-page presentation, fit/zoom and appropriate reading direction.
  • Efficient image loading, saved progress and supported bookmarks.
  • Supported archive and compression variations will be confirmed after testing.
03

Organization, then connection

Planned

After the expanded format foundation: Smart Library and organization first, followed by Calibre integration.

Library organization

Tags and Smart Library

Add user-defined tags and collections that fill themselves using rules, built around one logical library.

More about this direction
  • Tag editing, filtering and search.
  • Potential rules for author, title, tags, format, reading status and available metadata.
  • Organization should preserve book identity and reading data.

Library organization

More ways to find and organize books

Develop combined filters, better sorting and useful saved views for larger collections.

More about this direction
  • Explore bulk metadata editing and better metadata inspection.
  • Make relationships between multiple linked files easier to understand. Multiple files linked to one book do not necessarily have identical contents.
  • Keep organization efficient as the library grows, without repeated full scans.

Library integration

Calibre, after the library foundation

Bring useful Calibre-managed books and metadata into Aflow Read after tags and organization are established.

More about this direction
  • Explore practical import or transfer workflows, metadata, tags, authors and series.
  • The mechanism is undecided: file/export workflows or compatible server access may be considered.
  • No promise of wireless bidirectional sync, metadata editing or full Calibre library control. Calibre will not be required for basic use.
04

Longer-term possibilities

Exploring

Directions we want to investigate. Inclusion here is not a promise that every capability will ship.

Cross-device reading

Optional Apple-device synchronization

Explore progress, bookmarks, collections, preferences and library restoration across supported Apple devices. Cross-device library and reading-state sync is not part of the initial release.

More about this direction
  • Keep synchronization optional and basic local reading independent.
  • Preserve meaningful local reading state when sessions diverge; let the reader choose an opening position without silently destroying the alternative.
  • Automatic synchronization of every file or setting is not promised. Accessing files in iCloud Drive is different from syncing your library and reading state.

Reading experience

More ways to make reading yours

Explore richer themes, presets, typography choices, layout controls and accessibility options.

More about this direction
  • Build on the existing appearance tools.
  • Future scope and availability will be decided after design and qualification.

Reading insights

Reading insights that respect privacy

Explore helpful reading history, time, habits and progress summaries without invasive tracking or required external analytics.

More about this direction
  • Useful personal information rather than a requirement to share reading activity.
  • Specific metrics and data handling are not yet announced.

Reading experience

Keep improving everyday reading

Continue work on navigation, chapter transitions, complex EPUBs, image-heavy books, accessibility and supported language or reading-direction scenarios.

More about this direction
  • Prioritize demonstrated reader needs and verified improvements.
  • Preserve reading positions and library integrity as the experience evolves.

A priority in every phase

A growing library should still feel like yours.

Responsiveness is a continuing priority across every phase: fast browsing, efficient cover loading and updates that focus on changed books. We are building for larger personal collections without promising a fixed book-count or device-performance guarantee.

What would make your library feel more yours?

Tell us about the reading or library problem you want to solve. Ideas help shape priorities; they are not promises of a particular release.
